decisive_items: initial diagnosis was transient ischemic attack of the vertebrobasilar system
fatigue test and a neostigmine test were both negative
response.rationale: Episodic slurred speech with negative fatigue/neostigmine tests and vascular imaging showing vertebrobasilar stenosis strongly support TIA of the vertebrobasilar system; R3 is a near-duplicate label, while other candidates are broader or lack specific evidence.

rejected.why: Symptoms are transient, not persistent, and no acute infarct on MRI; stroke is less specific.
Too broad; lacks the vertebrobasilar localization supported by imaging.
Vertebrobasilar insufficiency is a mechanism, but TIA is the clinical diagnosis; imaging supports stenosis but not insufficiency as a distinct entity.
No evidence of vasculitis; MRI/MRA unremarkable except arteriosclerosis, and inflammatory markers normal.
Cerebral vasculopathy is descriptive of arteriosclerosis but not the episodic clinical syndrome; TIA is more accurate.
